```
9. A04-7: Calling the capture capability with a matching implementation and any
   facts-only file reference, empty or non-empty, alone or among readable
   refs, refuses naming its port and FileFactsRef without looking up inputs,
   reading input bytes, publishing bytes or recording a change. An unknown
   implementation still raises unknown_reference, and a contract mismatch
   still wins before the input refusal. Several facts-only refs name the
   smallest port, independent of tuple order.
   [witness: verification:kernel_a04_capture_file_facts_refused]
statements:
A04-7: capture(unknown_implementation, any_inputs) -> unknown_reference
       capture(contract_mismatch, any_inputs) -> refused_before_input_checks
       capture(matching_implementation, inputs_containing_FileFactsRef)
         -> refused AND no_input_lookup AND no_input_byte_read AND no_publication AND no_change
```

quotes: assert kind in {"implementation", "contract_version"}, "R11: looked up input before facts-only refusal"
assert lookups or kind == "implementation", "R11: implementation lookup was not first"
raise AssertionError("R11: read input bytes, published bytes, or recorded a change")
assert scenario == "unknown" and error is missing
assert scenario != "unknown", "R11: facts refusal hid unknown implementation"
assert "contract_version_id" in reason and "FileFactsRef" not in reason
assert ("beta" if scenario == "order" else "unreadable") in reason, reason
raise AssertionError("R11: accepted facts-only capture input")
verdicts.why: The selected parametrized tests cover empty and nonempty FileFactsRef values alone and at every position among readable references, detect input lookups, byte reads, publication, and change recording, and require refusal naming FileFactsRef and its port. They also verify unknown implementation precedence, contract-mismatch precedence, and—under both tuple orders—that the refusal names the lexically smallest port, beta.
